Contributing to Riemann

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Kisung You maintains Riemann, reviews changes, and prepares releases. Questions, examples that reveal unexpected results, corrections to documentation, and code contributions are welcome. Support is provided as time permits.

Ask a question or report a problem

Search the issue tracker first. If an existing discussion does not address your question, open an issue. Include the smallest example that reproduces the behavior, the result you expected, the result you obtained, and the output of sessionInfo(). For a GitHub installation, include the commit if known. You can use simulated data to reproduce a problem with a private dataset.

For a numerical issue, specify the manifold, geometry, and algorithm. Include the random seed, the termination message or diagnostics when available, and a reference value or calculation if you have one. For installation problems, include the installation command and the first error in its output.

Propose and test a change

Fork the repository, clone your fork, and create a branch from master. Use R 4.4 or later and a working compiler for R packages. The installation instructions link to tools for each operating system. Install the development dependencies from an R session at the repository root:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)
devtools::test()
devtools::check(cran = TRUE, run_dont_test = TRUE, error_on = "warning")

The check builds the package and its vignettes and runs the extended examples. Rendering the vignettes requires Pandoc, also supplied by RStudio. For work on a single test file, for example tests/testthat/test-kmeans.R, use devtools::test(filter = "kmeans") during development. Include a regression case for a numerical fix. A result calculated independently, a closed-form example, or an appropriate geometric invariance can make the test informative across platforms.

Edit function help in the roxygen comments in R/ and regenerate it with devtools::document(). For changes to the public method inventory, follow the maintenance instructions. To rebuild the website, install pkgdown, install the current checkout with devtools::install(), and run Rscript pkgdown/build.R from its root.

Open a pull request that explains the user-visible change, links any relevant issue, and states how you checked the result. If you propose changing a geometric convention or a public interface, start an issue to discuss the effect on existing analyses. The maintainer reviews proposals and uses the package checks on Linux, macOS, and Windows to inform merge decisions.
